categories.label: Input readiness
categories.summary: All 13 current NFL games meet the same eight-layer input-completeness standard used by the CFB model. This is a readiness score, not prediction accuracy or betting confidence.

items.title: Eight required layers
items.detail: Base stats, opponent adjustment, advanced efficiency, injuries/personnel, weather, market, travel/rest and depth chart are present for all 13 Week 6 games.

items.title: How the 90% rule works
items.detail: Eight equally weighted layers are worth 12.5% each, so a nominal 90% minimum effectively requires all eight layers. The current NFL slate is 8/8 on every game.

items.title: What remains unresolved
items.detail: Input readiness does not clear final inactives, remaining roof/weather decisions, account-level executable prices or prospective recommendation calibration. Those remain separate game-day and release gates.

categories.label: Injuries & availability
categories.summary: Official Week 6 status reports are refreshed. Confirmed hard-QB breaks remain Baltimore with Tyler Huntley, Philadelphia with Tanner McKee and Tampa Bay with Jalon Daniels; Caleb Williams is expected back for Chicago pending final active status.

items.title: Confirmed hard-QB breaks
items.detail: Lamar Jackson, Jalen Hurts and Baker Mayfield are out. Their replacement states are treated as reliability/release events; the operational QB point adjustment remains zero because an additive coefficient has not been prospectively validated.

items.title: Final inactives
items.detail: Official inactive lists are still checked close to kickoff and can change contextual reliability without rewriting the frozen canonical projection.

items.title: Personnel discipline
items.detail: Non-QB absences and questionable designations are recorded as context unless a historically validated numerical adjustment exists.

categories.label: Weather & venue
categories.summary: Weather and venue context has been refreshed for the full slate. Tampa carries the clearest elevated wind uncertainty; Indianapolis has confirmed the Lucas Oil Stadium roof and window open.

items.title: London
items.detail: Wembley is cool with a moderate breeze/gust and shower-variability profile; it remains a game-day context gate rather than a discretionary point adjustment.

items.title: Tampa
items.detail: Raymond James Stadium carries elevated wind with sustained northeast flow and stronger gusts. Reliability is flagged, but the frozen total is not rewritten.

items.title: Roof status
items.detail: Indianapolis has confirmed the roof and window open. Atlanta's game-specific retractable-roof decision remains pending; SoFi and Allegiant are treated as covered/indoor venues.

categories.label: Market comparison
categories.summary: The NFL projection remains independent of sportsbook lines. The full Week 6 board was refreshed from Action Network public game pages at 7:55 AM ET; these are comparison benchmarks, not verified executable account prices.

items.title: Current benchmark
items.detail: All 13 remaining Week 6 games now use a single game-day Action Network public benchmark source and timestamp for spread/total comparison.

items.title: Model / market difference
items.detail: A numerical difference is descriptive research only. Historical testing did not support a simple larger-difference-equals-better-edge rule.

items.title: Consensus test
items.detail: A walk-forward model-plus-market blend was tested previously. The optimal historical solution collapsed to the market itself, so no market-consensus model layer was promoted.

categories.label: Efficiency & architecture
categories.summary: The spread model uses only feature families that survived leakage-safe out-of-sample testing; the totals model remains deliberately simpler.

items.title: Canonical spread
items.detail: Frozen core efficiency plus validated defensive coverage, market-independent recursive win Elo and margin rating.

items.title: Canonical total
items.detail: Frozen core totals architecture. Pace, red-zone and other tested additions did not earn robust promotion.

items.title: FTN50
items.detail: FTN50 remains a shadow/challenger model and cannot silently replace the canonical projection without explicit promotion review.

categories.label: Validation
categories.summary: Historical research validation is complete, but betting recommendation thresholds remain locked while prospective frozen-week evidence accumulates.

items.title: Historical sample
items.detail: The canonical architecture has 816 outer out-of-sample games from 2023-2025.

items.title: Win probability
items.detail: Canonical-margin win probability passed the separate walk-forward research-display calibration gate. Moneyline edge remains HOLD.

items.title: Prospective milestones
items.detail: Research/Beta review begins at 40+ completed prospective games across at least 3 frozen weeks; recommendation calibration review begins at 75+ games across at least 5 weeks and still requires explicit review.

categories.label: Weekly production workflow
categories.summary: Each week uses an immutable prediction freeze followed by separate context, market, grading and registry updates.

items.title: Pregame freeze
items.detail: Canonical and challenger projections are timestamped before games and are never rewritten after results are known.

items.title: Game-day gates
items.detail: Starting QB, final inactives, weather/roof and fresh public market benchmarks are refreshed separately from the frozen numerical prediction.

items.title: Postgame grading
items.detail: Canonical and FTN50 are graded on identical games, then the prospective registry updates model-health and release-calibration evidence.
